weaknesses.title: Theorem 1 is only a finite computation, yet is presented as a closed-form theorem for general odd w
weaknesses.detail: The 'proof' is a case-by-case exact computation for 3 ≤ w ≤ 61. No general argument establishes the closed forms f_w = 3((w-1)/2)!/w and g_w = 6|B_{w-1}|/((w-1)/2)!. The general statement is relegated to Conjecture 1. The title, abstract and the phrase 'closed forms' therefore overstate what is shown. The paper itself lists a binomial-sum proof as an open question. The formula is essentially a pattern fit to computed data, with additional dependence on unverified inputs.
weaknesses.suggestion: Retitle and reframe as a computer-assisted verification of a conjectured closed form for 3 ≤ w ≤ 61. State the general-w result explicitly as a conjecture in the abstract and title. Say clearly that Theorem 1 is a finite verification, not a derivation.

weaknesses.title: Proof rests on two unchecked and insufficiently specified external ingredients
weaknesses.detail: Step 3 depends on Theorem 5.1 of D'Hoker-Kaidi, which is not machine-checked. The 'transcription' check against their eq. 5.19 is only a consistency check. Step 2 relies on a 'standard lemma' (harmonic + SL(2,Z)-invariant + polynomial growth implies constant) that is never stated precisely. The relevant hypotheses are the exact growth condition and the behaviour of the Laplace kernel, since the Laplacian kernel on the fundamental domain also contains non-constant solutions unless growth is controlled. The Laurent-polynomial statement is used for a combination built from several C(a,b,c), and it is unclear how the DGV combination's Laurent expansion is assembled. This is the load-bearing part of the argument and it is not reproducible from the text.
weaknesses.suggestion: State the lemma and the D'Hoker-Kaidi theorem precisely, with hypotheses, and show that they apply to X_w. Give a worked Laurent-constant computation (e.g. w = 5 or 7) in the text. A fully independent check of the constant, such as the exact values of g_w against the numerics for all w ≤ 17, would also help. Machine-checking the lemma is optional but desirable.

weaknesses.title: Theorem 2 (uniqueness) is under-specified and the exact verification is not shown
weaknesses.detail: The space {X : ΔX ∈ Q E(w)} is never defined: the ambient basis (all C(a,b,c) of weight w? with products of Eisenstein series?) is not specified. The claim of dimension 1 for odd w and 0 for even w, for 3 ≤ w ≤ 25, is supported only by the assertion that exact computation was done. The Certificate also says the statement and the combination X_w are 'known', so the novelty is unclear. The statement of Theorem 2 as written ('For odd w it is spanned by the DGV combination') omits the even case and the range. In addition, dimension 0 for even w is stated while the constant-term (ζ) bookkeeping for the relation space is not discussed.
weaknesses.suggestion: Define the ambient space and basis precisely, state the full theorem including range and the even case, and give the rank computation data (matrix sizes, ranks) in an appendix. Clarify what is new relative to DGV.

weaknesses.title: Inconsistencies and errors in the presentation of results and numerics
weaknesses.detail: Several statements are inconsistent or unclear. Theorem 1 is stated with the normalisation ΔX_w = w(w−1) f_w E(w), but Table 1 and Examples use different normalisations: Example 2 writes 30C(2,2,1) − 12E(5) − ζ(5) = 0, which is X/(g_w) scaling, and Table 2 gives integer-normalised coefficients with no mapping back to f_w, g_w. Weight 9 is called a 'Numerical observation' although the paper claims it exactly. Table 1 values (e.g. f_w, g_w at w = 13: g = 691/327600) are not obviously consistent with the closed form displayed (a sample check is needed, e.g. |B_12| = 691/2730 gives 6·691/(2730·720)=691/327600, which is consistent, but this is never shown). Remark 1 and the abstract disagree on which weights are covered by exact versus numerical evidence. The text also claims 'no earlier test point was affected' by a bug while a residual of 3.5e-10 was seen at τ1 = 1/4. The statement of the Laplace equation at w = 11 has a coefficient 100 E(11) whereas the formula with f_11 = 360/11 would give a different normalisation, which is unexplained. Fig. 1 refers to a 'conjectured' line and 'blind test' while the text calls w ≤ 61 proved.
weaknesses.suggestion: Provide one explicit conversion from the integer-normalised relations to (f_w, g_w), show the check of Table 1 against the closed form, and unify the use of 'theorem', 'observation' and 'conjecture'. Resolve the bug-report wording and the w = 11 normalisation.

weaknesses.title: Novelty, attribution and exposition are weak; document reads as auto-generated
weaknesses.detail: The key identities for w = 3, 5, 7, 9 are known, and for w = 11 the combination is known; the genuinely new content is the constants for w ≥ 11 and the closed-form guess. The 'novelty status' entries and the laboratory-workflow material (agent roles, red-team counts, provenance tables, 'preregistered' tests with n = 1) take space but add little scientific value. The Introduction and Setting are fragmentary (the lattice-sum definition of C(a,b,c) and E(w) is missing, 'Setting' refers to a normalisation that is not shown, and DGV eq. 3.57 is not reproduced), so the paper is not self-contained. The appendix contains unrelated material (eta quotients, theta/E8 identities, M4(Γ0(N)) tables, Figs. 3) that is irrelevant to the main claim. Claims such as 'preregistered blind test' for a pattern that is then verified by the same pipeline overstate the independence of the check, and the verifier uses its own code with a known bug history. Acknowledging AI-assisted generation is good, but authorship and responsibility ('the authors') are inconsistent with a single listed author.
weaknesses.suggestion: Make the paper self-contained by defining C(a,b,c), E(w), X_w explicitly, and state clearly what is new. Remove or move the unrelated eta-quotient/theta material and the lab-process statistics. Temper the 'blind test' language, and cite the literature more carefully for the w = 11 and w = 13 cases.
